Third Quarter 2026 Highlights

  • Revenue from new business accounted for 14% of net revenue
  • Local revenue, including digital packages sold locally, accounted for 76% of net revenue and declined 6% year-over-year
  • Digital revenue was $9.8 million, down 24% year-over-year and down 12% on a same-station basis 
  • Digital revenue accounted for 23% of net revenue, or 24% of net revenue, excluding political  
  • Digital segment operating margin was 32%, up from 21% in Q3'25

During the third quarter of 2026, Beasley continued to advance its strategic priorities of rebuilding core revenue, expanding digital profitability, and strengthening its balance sheet through disciplined deleveraging and portfolio optimization. Building on the comprehensive debt restructuring completed in May, the Company raised gross proceeds of approximately $4.6 million through a registered direct offering and concurrent private placement in September. Subsequent to quarter-end, Beasley completed the sale of two radio stations and two parcels of real estate, generating more than $10 million in net proceeds for the four assets sold. These actions further strengthened the Company's financial position, reducing the outstanding principal amount of first-lien notes to approximately $3.6 million and providing additional flexibility to execute its long-term operating strategy.

Net revenue during the three months ended September 30, 2026 of $42.8 million decreased 16.1%, or 10.2% on a same-station basis, reflecting continued weakness in traditional national and local agency advertising. These declines were partially offset by a 7% increase in local direct revenue on a same-station basis and contributions from political advertising. Digital revenue declined 12.3% on a same-station basis during the quarter, although year-to-date same-station digital revenue increased 4.4%. Importantly, digital operating margins expanded to approximately 32%, compared with 21% (or 26% on a same-station basis) in the prior-year period, reflecting continued progress toward a more efficient, higher-margin digital business.

Operating expenses, excluding corporate expenses, depreciation and amortization, declined approximately $7.0 million, or 15.1% year-over-year, reflecting the continued benefits of structural cost reduction initiatives implemented over the past two years. On a same-station basis, operating expenses declined approximately $3.7 million. The third quarter reflected a more complete benefit from the Company's most recent expense reduction initiatives implemented in May 2026, demonstrating the ongoing impact of its efforts to establish a more efficient and sustainable operating model.

Station Operating Income totaled approximately $3.6 million, representing an SOI margin of 8.5%. Corporate expenses totaled approximately $3.9 million, compared with $2.2 million in the prior-year period, reflecting restructuring, financing, and strategic transaction-related costs, as well as the absence of a prior-year franchise tax benefit. Excluding applicable nonrecurring items, corporate expenses were approximately $2.8 million.

Adjusted EBITDA was approximately $1.3 million for the third quarter of 2026, compared with $3.9 million in the prior-year period. While profitability continued to reflect pressure from lower advertising revenue, the Company's structural expense reductions meaningfully reduced the impact on operating performance.

Commenting on the financial results, Caroline Beasley, Chief Executive Officer, said:

"While the advertising environment remains challenging, our third-quarter results demonstrate the tangible progress we are making in building a more efficient and financially resilient company. The structural cost reductions implemented over the past two years are helping us protect profitability amid continued revenue pressure, while our digital business is generating stronger operating margins. We are encouraged by the growth in local direct advertising and remain focused on rebuilding revenue, improving sales productivity, and expanding the higher-margin products and services that we believe will support sustainable growth."

"Looking ahead, our priorities remain clear: stabilize and rebuild core revenue, expand digital profitability, improve free cash flow generation, and continue reducing leverage. While there is more work ahead, we believe the actions we have taken have established a stronger operating and financial foundation. As we enter the next phase of our transformation, we remain focused on translating these improvements into more consistent financial performance and creating long-term value for our stockholders."

About Beasley Broadcast Group

The Company is a multi-platform media company whose primary business is operating radio stations throughout the United States. The Company offers local and national advertisers integrated marketing solutions across audio, digital and event platforms. The Company owns and operates 47 AM and FM stations in the following large- and mid-size markets in the United States: Augusta, GA, Boston, MA, Charlotte, NC, Detroit, MI, Fayetteville, NC, Las Vegas, NV, Middlesex, NJ, Monmouth, NJ, Morristown, NJ, Philadelphia, PA, and Tampa-Saint Petersburg, FL. Approximately 17 million consumers listen to the Company's radio stations weekly over-the-air, online and on smartphones and tablets, and millions regularly engage with the Company's brands and personalities through digital platforms such as Facebook, X, text, apps and email. For more information, please visit www.bbgi.com.

For further information, or to receive future Beasley Broadcast Group news announcements via e-mail, please contact Beasley Broadcast Group, at 239-263-5000 or ir@bbgi.com.

Definitions

EBITDA is defined as net income (loss) before interest income or expense, income tax expense or benefit, depreciation, and amortization.

Adjusted EBITDA is defined as EBITDA further adjusted to exclude certain non-operating or other items that we believe are not indicative of the performance of our ongoing operations, such as impairment losses, other income or expense, one-time severance expense, stock-based compensation or equity in earnings of unconsolidated affiliates, gains on dispositions and gain on debt restructure. See "Reconciliation of Net Income (Loss) to Adjusted EBITDA" for additional information.

Adjusted EBITDA is a measure widely used in the media industry. The Company recognizes that because Adjusted EBITDA is not calculated in accordance with GAAP, it is not necessarily comparable to similarly titled measures employed by other companies. However, management believes that Adjusted EBITDA provides meaningful information to investors because it is an important measure of how effectively we operate our business and assists investors in comparing our operating performance with that of other media companies.

Same station revenue and same station operating expenses exclude revenue or operating expenses, as applicable, from all divestitures and other operations that were exited in the prior 12 months. These measures provide investors with a clearer view of core business performance by eliminating the impact of portfolio changes and enabling more meaningful year-over-year comparisons. By isolating the performance of continuing operations, same station results offer greater transparency into underlying trends, operational execution, and the effectiveness of strategic initiative.

New business revenue is defined as revenue from an advertiser that has not advertised in the prior 13 months before the start of the current quarter.

data.title: American Fusion Inc. (OTCQB: AMFN) Reports Third Quarter 2026 Results and $1.55 Million in Year-To-Date Financing
data.description:
Stockholders’ deficit narrowed 34% from June 30. The Company converted $987,000 of accrued compensation to equity and appointed Brent Nelson as Chief Executive Officer

SOUTHLAKE, Texas, Nov. 13, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- American Fusion Inc. OTCQB:AMFN (“American Fusion” or the “Company”), developer of the proprietary Texatron™ Fusion Engine™, today announced the filing of its Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026. The Company also highlighted financial, operational and corporate progress during the quarter and in recent weeks.

During the third quarter, American Fusion strengthened its balance sheet and grew its intellectual property portfolio. It also invested in research and testing equipment and converted most of its accrued compensation obligations into long-term equity. After the quarter ended, the Company completed a leadership transition. It also raised additional capital as it prepares for the next phase of Texatron™ development and testing.

Third Quarter and Year-to-Date 2026 Financial Highlights

$1.55 million in financing year-to-date: Net cash provided by financing activities was $1,551,000 for the nine months ended September 30, 2026. This consisted of $1,071,000 from the Company’s fixed-price prepaid warrant facility and $480,000 from the sale of equity units to third-party investors at $0.05 to $0.07 per unit. Each unit included a warrant exercisable at $0.50 per share. Prepaid warrant funding in the third quarter alone totaled $446,000.

Total assets nearly doubled: Total assets increased to $372,313 at September 30, 2026, from $196,683 at June 30, 2026.

Liabilities reduced: Total liabilities declined approximately 21% to $1,473,333 at September 30, 2026, from $1,856,662 at June 30, 2026.

Stockholders’ deficit improved 34%: Total stockholders’ deficit improved to $(1,101,020) at September 30, 2026, from $(1,659,980) at June 30, 2026.

Patent portfolio expansion: Capitalized patent filing costs reached $166,992 for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $33,472 at June 30. This reflects a significant increase in new patent filings covering the Texatron™ platform.

Investment in testing infrastructure: The Company capitalized $44,169 of research and development testing equipment acquired for future projects.

Continued R&D investment: Research and development expense was $112,195 for the third quarter and $243,538 for the nine-month period.

Non-cash expense profile: Of the $1,399,778 in third quarter operating expenses, $764,752 (approximately 55%) was non-cash stock-based compensation, primarily for officer, director and advisory agreements.

Capital Structure and Governance

$986,958 of accrued compensation converted to equity: Effective September 30, 2026, twelve officers, directors, consultants and advisors agreed to exchange their rights to common stock compensation for newly designated Series C Convertible Preferred Stock. The exchange removed $986,958 of accrued compensation obligations and replaced them with equity. Series C shares generally cannot be converted into common stock until the later of full vesting and the earlier of (i) the 20th trading day after a national exchange listing or (ii) nine months after issuance. After that, conversions are spread over four quarters.

Share count held steady: Common shares outstanding were 1,619,034,363 at September 30, 2026. That is unchanged from June 30 and approximately 45% below the 2,954,801,029 shares outstanding at December 31, 2025. The reduction follows the court-ordered cancellation of 1.683 billion legacy shares earlier in the year.

Board strengthened: John Gerdin joined the Board of Directors on August 11, 2026. He brings board governance, corporate finance and capital markets experience.

Texas DSHS registration: On July 17, 2026, the Company received Certificate of Registration No. R54726 from the Texas Department of State Health Services. The registration covers twelve registered Texatron™ Fusion Engine™ research model classes ranging from 500 kW to 1 GW, for research and development activities at its authorized testing location in Lubbock, Texas. It remains effective through February 28, 2034. The registration authorizes research and development activities only and does not constitute certification of the Company’s technology or commercial performance.

Recent Developments

Leadership transition: On October 26, 2026, Brent Nelson, Executive Chairman since March 1, 2026, was appointed Chief Executive Officer and continues as Chairman of the Board. Richard C. Hawkins, the former Chief Executive Officer, was appointed Chief Administrative Officer.

Additional capital: In late October 2026, the Company received aggregate net financing of approximately $687,000 for the acquisition of a property for testing.

data.title: S&P 500, Nasdaq end lower as Nvidia uncertainty weighs on tech shares
data.description:
Key points:
  • Microsoft edges up after global outage eases
  • October producer prices rise 6.5% year over year, Labor Department says
  • Nvidia shares fall for sixth straight week, longest losing streak since October 2012

By Chuck Mikolajczak and Niket Nishant

The S&P 500 and Nasdaq closed lower on Friday, as concerns about Nvidia pressured technology shares, while a reading on inflation failed to alter expectations for more rate hikes from the Federal Reserve.

Nvidia's shares fell and recorded their sixth straight week of declines, their longest streak since October 2012, after CEO Jensen Huang's resignation on Thursday. He stepped down after revelations of extramarital affairs, including a relationship with a businesswoman suspected by the US of spying for China.

The Financial Times reported that Nvidia's board has approached British chipmaker Arm Holdings CEO Rene Haas in its search for a potential successor to Huang.

The uncertainty about leadership at the chipmaker has raised concerns about the durability of the AI trade, given Nvidia's primary role in the industry's boom and its financial ties to a host of companies in the sector, which has been a pillar of the bull market in equities.

"The tech trade, the AI trade, Nvidia is going to go through a period of volatility, and you're going to see the bulls and bears kind of wrestle on where this narrative goes through the rest of the year ... there's been a loss of confidence," said Anthony Saglimbene, chief market strategist at Ameriprise Financial in Troy, Michigan.

"The market and investors are trying to navigate what does the AI theme look like when we have the absence of Jensen Huang, who was basically the AI champion and willing to use Nvidia's balance sheet to fund a lot of this AI expansion. That's gone."

According to preliminary data, the S&P 500 CBOE:SPX lost 31.53 points, or 0.42%, to end at 7,560.87 points, while the Nasdaq Composite lost 230.13 points, or 0.91%, to 25,135.96. The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 46.14 points, or 0.09%, to 52,343.23.

Despite the recent volatility, the major indexes recorded weekly gains, as the Nasdaq and S&P 500 both snapped a four-week streak of declines.

The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell, with Advanced Micro Devices and Broadcom the biggest drags.

Neoclouds CoreWeave and Nebius also ended lower, while data center-related firms IREN and Applied Digital retreated as well.

The losses come ahead of AI company Anthropic's much-anticipated IPO next week, which could test investor appetite for established AI heavyweights as money potentially shifts toward the new entrant.

The S&P 500 technology index was the worst-performing of the 11 major S&P sectors. But Microsoft ended higher, erasing earlier declines, after a global outage that included its Outlook and Teams products began to ease.

INFLATION CONCERNS REMAIN

On the economic front, the Labor Department said US producer prices were slightly cooler than expected in October, but still shot up 6.5% year over year, the largest annual gain since November 2022.

The data kept expectations for a rate hike of at least 25 basis points at the Fed's December meeting completely locked in, with markets pricing in a roughly 10% chance for an outsized 50-basis-point increase, according to CME FedWatch.

Comments from multiple Fed officials earlier this week suggested the US central bank was open to a more aggressive path of rate hikes as price pressures worsen.

The sentiment for additional rate hikes was echoed by more Fed officials on Friday, including San Francisco Federal Reserve President Mary Daly, who said her "bias" is that the central bank will need to increase its policy rate, while Boston Federal Reserve President Susan Collins said tighter monetary policy is coming because of high inflation.

data.title: Son of ex-CIA chief Brennan charged over sexual images of minor girls
data.description:
Key points:
  • Complaint alleges FBI phone review found 88 suspected child pornography images
  • Complaint says investigation began in 2024 after tip to child protection group
  • Virginia authorities searched Kyle Brennan's home in July 2024, complaint says

By Jana Winter and Andrew Goudsward

The son of former CIA Director John Brennan was charged on Friday with "transportation of child pornography," according to court documents and a US law enforcement official.

Kyle Brennan, of Warrenton, Virginia, was charged after an FBI review of his cellphone found 88 images that appeared to depict minor girls engaged in sexually explicit conduct, according to a criminal complaint filed in US District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia.

John Brennan is a longtime antagonist of President Donald Trump, and the Justice Department has been investigating the former CIA director for more than a year.

A criminal complaint showed the investigation into Kyle Brennan began independently of the probe into his father, which has been dubbed by both proponents and detractors the “grand conspiracy” probe.

The complaint said the investigation into the younger Brennan originated in 2024 with a tip from the software company Adobe to the National Center for Missing & Exploited Children, a child protection organization.

Virginia authorities searched his home in July 2024, and the case was referred to the FBI last month, according to the criminal complaint.

Kyle Brennan was under arrest, and his attorney did not immediately respond to a request for comment. A spokesperson for John Brennan declined to comment.

John Brennan, who led the CIA during Democratic President Barack Obama’s administration, has been scrutinized as part of a wider probe examining whether law enforcement and intelligence officials violated Trump’s civil rights in prior investigations of the president.

The conspiracy investigation has stalled in recent weeks following the resignations of senior prosecutors who had been overseeing it. No charges have so far been brought.

John Brennan has denied wrongdoing and his lawyers have accused prosecutors of improperly targeting Brennan at Trump’s direction.

The former CIA director was subpoenaed to testify before a grand jury last month, but his appearance was postponed after Joseph diGenova, a DOJ official who had been leading the investigation, resigned in September.

data.title: SA Asks: Is Nvidia a buy, sell or hold after Jensen Huang's departure?
data.description:
Is Nvidia a buy, sell, or hold following the departure of CEO and co-founder Jensen Huang amid allegations that he had affairs with two co-workers and suspected Chinese spy?

Seeking Alpha analysts Kenio Fontes, Dhierin Bechai, The Techie, and Danil Sereda weigh in.

Kenio Fontes: Before the news of the second affair and that Jensen Huang was really leaving Nvidia , I wrote this in a macro piece: “Even without Jensen Huang (which indeed is important for the company), Nvidia could be a buy at 11x forward earnings.”

Jensen Huang was a key asset for the company, and he’ll be difficult to replace, no doubt about it. Also, we have other uncertainties related to customers and internal organization.

Yet, the market itself is already making a point here. Even after all the chaos, the stock dropped from $188 to $150, then rebounded to $168. The discount related to this uncertainty is around 10%, and in my view, the main reason is that Nvidia is already cheap enough. There is real and new uncertainty in the story, but Nvidia is still a wide moat company (CUDA, switching costs, scale, strong partnerships, etc.) with solid prospects. The valuation is just the icing on the cake.

In short, I’d summarize it as a cautious Buy. The price is compelling enough, and even without Huang, Nvidia should be able to generate decent shareholder returns. Yet, caution is also warranted, as we don’t know how further regulation, competition, and changes in management and strategic vision could affect the short- and long-term thesis.

Dhierin Bechai: I still believe Nvidia is a Buy. It may take some time for investors to regain trust in the company, but generally we see companies rebound from forced CEO transitions.

The flat architecture of Nvidia can provide a challenge, and Nvidia has to find a fitting reporting structure for the next CEO while maintaining an agile position. While there are many uncertainties and Nvidia’s architect is now gone, I do believe that with a talented workforce and hopefully a CEO with engineering or scientific experience, Nvidia should remain innovative with in-demand solutions supporting the Buy rating.

Competitors such as Advanced Micro Devices , Marvell , Intel , and Broadcom cannot all of a sudden fill any demand that would move away from Nvidia if customers have concerns about the company. So, I don’t believe it is likely that we will see major growth disruptions in the coming years.

The main watch items right now are the company's response to the situation during the upcoming earnings call, a permanent CEO selection, and market reaction, including money rotation into Nvidia's competitors.

(Dhierin Bechai leads the SA investing group The Aerospace Forum.)

The Techie: I’m maintaining Nvidia with a Hold. While the stock has pulled back 27% over the past month, and a lot of the negatives are priced in, I think uncertainty is something the market doesn’t buy into. Earnings are on the 17th, and the new interim CEO, Colette Kress, will host a company meeting the next day. Until then, I think investors should stay on the sidelines and tread carefully, as I would not be surprised to hear of a fourth allegation.

Danil Sereda: There should be another CEO shortly, and while the whole market is waiting for the right person to appear, the stock's valuation will be in question. In other words, NVDA is currently priced at ~10.5x forward earnings (fiscal FY2028), which is dramatically low for the expected 70% EPS growth rate on a year-over-year basis for that fiscal year. But it can drop by another 10-15% as the market keeps deciding the size of Jensen's premium in the past.

For me, Nvidia is a Buy, although I admit the risk I described above. I'd target a P/E of 15-20x on FY2028 EPS eventually, just as I wrote in my previous article - even without any premiums on top of what's currently expected as the base-case EPS figure for that year. In that case, NVDA is getting a price target of ~$278.41/share.

(Danil Sereda leads the SA investing group Beyond the Wall Investing.)

data.title: Crude Futures Post Back-to-Back Weekly Losses — 2nd Update
data.description:
By Farhan Rafid and Anthony Harrup

Oil futures fell for a second consecutive week, while traders assessed the International Energy Agency's outlook for a global supply surplus, continued disruptions to Middle Eastern oil shipments, and cooling expectations for a negotiated settlement between the U.S. and Iran.

Front-month Brent crude for January delivery settled at $95.84 a barrel on Friday, up two cents on the day and down 2.5% from a week ago. West Texas Intermediate for December delivery slipped 0.2% to $88.56 a barrel for a 2.5% weekly loss.

The International Energy Agency said Friday that the global oil market is expected to return to a surplus in the fourth quarter for the first time since the Iran war began, as a recovery in Middle Eastern exports outpaces demand.

Global oil supply rose by 2.3 million barrels a day to 105.4 million barrels a day in October, prompting the Paris-based agency to raise its fourth-quarter supply estimate by 3.3 million barrels a day. Gulf oil exports excluding Oman reached 18.4 million barrels a day, about 26% below prewar levels.

The agency also reported the first monthly increase in observed global oil inventories since June, with stocks rising by 52 million barrels in October. However, inventories remained 462 million barrels below their levels at the start of the war.

Oil futures rebounded Thursday after President Trump said Washington no longer needed an agreement with Iran, raising questions about the prospects for negotiations. Trump also said in a Truth Social post that the U.S. had secured control of the Strait of Hormuz.

"Oil prices have come off really quite significantly, even with the uptick of the last couple of days," said Ellen Fraser, a partner and energy analyst at consulting firm Baringa. But the decline has been sentiment-driven, which "in itself is a bit of a warning."

The northern hemisphere is heading for a tight winter with prices still well above pre-war levels, Fraser added. "There's still a lot of tension and stress in the market."

ING analysts said recovering Middle Eastern production had eased immediate supply concerns, although reliance on alternative export routes continued to leave shipments vulnerable to disruption. The pace at which traffic through the Strait of Hormuz returns to normal remains a key factor for oil prices, they said.

Oil markets may be pricing in the prospect of diplomatic progress before additional supplies become available, according to Terri-Leigh Bennett, chief operating officer at CMS Prime. Negotiations wouldn't immediately restore damaged infrastructure, normalize shipping routes or guarantee uninterrupted production, she said.

Security risks persisted across the region. The Bahrain-based Joint Maritime Information Center, a multinational maritime security monitoring body, said in an advisory distributed Thursday by U.K. Maritime Trade Operations that it had recorded 181 maritime security incidents since March 1, including four since its previous report published Sunday.

Oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz also remained sharply below prewar levels, with confirmed transits averaging 4.06 million barrels a day in the latest weekly data available Wednesday, compared with 17.1 million barrels a day before the conflict, according to preliminary Kpler data.

The IEA expects global oil demand to fall by 2.7 million barrels a day this year before rebounding by 2 million barrels a day in 2027. It warned that further attacks on shipping could undermine the recovery in oil flows.

data.title: Soybean futures set two-week high, wheat rises from June low
data.description:
By Tom Polansek

Chicago Board of Trade soybean futures set a two-week high on Friday and corn futures also advanced as traders refocused on tightened US supply forecasts.

US export demand helped support prices, traders said.

The US Department of Agriculture lowered its projection for 2026/27 soybean ending stocks in a monthly report on Tuesday, when analysts were expecting an increase, and raised its outlook for US exports. It also pegged US corn stocks below analysts' expectations.

"We're still digesting the report from earlier in the week," said Matt Wiegand, commodity broker for FuturesOne. "We got friendlier carryout numbers on corn and beans."

The USDA on Friday reported that exporters sold US soybeans to China, Vietnam and unknown destinations and US corn to Mexico. The agency separately said 2026/27 US corn export sales were 2.9 million metric tons for the week that ended on November 5, toward the high end of analysts' expectations.

CBOT January soybeans finished 12-1/2 cents higher at $12.31-1/2 per bushel and reached the highest level since October 30. December corn futures ended 3 cents higher at $4.45-1/2 per bushel.

Wheat also advanced, with December futures closing up 9 cents at $5.93-1/4 per bushel on the CBOT.

Technical buying helped lift wheat prices after the most-active contract touched its lowest level since June 30, traders said. Some traders said losses on Thursday had been overdone.

"Grains are bouncing strongly after yesterday's sharp selloff," said Andrey Sizov, head of consultancy Sovecon.

Traders monitored continued disruptions to Black Sea grain exports, despite diplomatic efforts to end Russia's war with Ukraine.

With no sign of progress in Russia-Ukraine talks toward a ceasefire in the Black Sea, limited shipments should support wheat prices, Sizov said. He added that competitively priced new-crop Argentine wheat could remain a cap on prices.

"If wheat starts flowing through the Black Sea, there's likely more downside for prices," said Rod Baker, an analyst at Bendigo Bank. "If it doesn't, we're getting close to a price floor now."

data.title: Raw sugar gains 1%, white sugar delivery is as expected
data.description:
Raw sugar futures on ICE rose on Friday to post a small weekly gain, with the market finally stabilising after its recent steady fall. Deliveries on the expiration of the spot white sugar contract were as expected at nearly 250,000 metric tons.

The CFTC report on traders' positioning was postponed to Monday due to the Veterans Day holiday.

SUGAR

* Raw sugar ​​settled up 0.19 cent, or 1%, at 18.41 cents per lb. The market had a small weekly gain of 1% after three consecutive weekly declines.

* Dealers said the market was underpinned by a drop in production in Brazil's key centre-south region this season, although weak demand continued to keep a lid on prices.

* They also noted a pickup in buying by China in the physical market.

* White sugar gained 0.9% to $514.40 a metric ton in the last trading day of the December contract (LSUZ6).

* Traders said deliveries against the contract's expiration totalled 244,900 tons, broadly in line with market expectations.

* ED&F Man Commodities was said to be the lone receiver of the sugar while Aditya Commodity Traders and Brazil's BTG were seen among the largest deliverers.

COFFEE

* Arabica coffee settled down 1.05 cent, or 0.4%, at $2.735 per lb. However, it gained 0.7% in the week after a run of three consecutive weekly declines.

* Dealers said supplies of arabica appeared to be improving, boosted partly by strong exports from Brazil, while exchange stocks have also begun to edge higher.

* Exchange stocks stood at 228,586 bags, as of November 12, up from 224,771 bags a week ago. At the same time last year, stocks stood at 404,930 bags.

* Robusta coffee fell 0.3% to $3,196 a ton, hovering just above last week's 2-1/2-year low of $3,140. The market lost 2% weekly.

COCOA

* London cocoa settled up £51, or 1.3%, to £4,037 per ton.

* New York cocoa rose 1.1% to $5,260 a ton.

* Both cocoa markets ended the week flat.

* Weak demand for chocolate has been weighing on prices, although there continue to be concerns that the El Nino weather pattern will curb global production.
